source.title: A Fully Probabilistic Perspective on Large Language Model Unlearning: Evaluation and Optimization
source.authors: Anda Cheng; Wei Huang; Ying-Gui Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests residual leakage from unlearned information using semantically rewritten inputs and multiple output samples, a different evaluation method aimed at the same question.
record.gate_note: The study reports a direct example where rephrasing a query elicits the forgotten answer, and evaluates unlearning methods under its fully probabilistic evaluation framework. Hyperparameter-selection and clustering details are not recorded as findings. The Harry Potter figure's plotted values are not numerically recoverable from the text.
record.test_reason: The study queries unlearned models with semantically rewritten prompts plus output sampling (FPE) and shows forgotten answers can resurface. This bears on E and on A's no-recovery part. It also proposes CEL as a method that resists related-query leakage, which bears on F.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude that FPE (rephrased inputs plus sampled outputs) reveals more residual leakage than greedy or output-only evaluation, and that CEL improves effectiveness and robustness while keeping utility. Note that CEL is evaluated only under the authors' own FPE.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Fully Probabilistic Evaluation with input-distribution sampling and a new Contrastive Embedding Loss; it does not reproduce the original unlearning recipes or the three original sources' attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Input-distribution choice changes the leakage evaluation; the study reports that FPE identifies risks missed by deterministic and output-only evaluation. CEL results also vary with contrast-center count, margin, and balance coefficient.

fits_no_version.finding: Output-only multinomial sampling reveals Harry Potter leakage that greedy decoding misses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sampling multiple outputs exposes residual leakage that deterministic decoding hides.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 2025
record.problems: The direct rephrasing demonstration is a single example. Quantitative Harry Potter results are shown only in a figure, without values in the text. TOFU leakage scores have no chance-level reference; the reported Sstd is a leakage metric rather than an uncertainty estimate. The paper notes that probabilistic evaluation and CEL can be computationally intensive and that scalability is a challenge.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted non-CEL method comparisons in Appendix Tables 4 and 5, CEL SED values for forget01 and forget10 in those tables, and utility metrics for non-CEL methods in Table 1. Hyperparameter ablations in Tables 2 and 3 and contrast-center sweeps in Figure 4 were also left out because they do not directly test the specified recovery attacks.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted accuracy, and general ability relative to the pre-unlearning model.
All parts: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All parts: no activation ablation or block-vs-delete analysis.
Jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information. Also rephrasing alone, separated from sampling, on TOFU at scale.
CEL is not tested against fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, jailbreaks, or other languages.

missing.what: Comparator Smean on forget10 for Phi-1.5 (GA 0.2096, RMU 0.2120), which are below CEL's 0.2382; the F limits_scope verdict rests on them. Rows_left_out declares them, but they are needed for the F verdict.

record.verdict_notes: TOFU FPE scores have no original-query or greedy baseline, so they cannot show how much rephrasing adds. The direct evidence for E is a single NPO example plus the Harry Potter figure. The paper's claim that CEL is best on all metrics holds for forget05 but not for Smean on forget10 Phi-1.5.

versions.untested_parts: No chance-accuracy reference is reported. The study does not establish that unlearning reaches near chance, and its examples and probabilistic evaluation do not test whether simple attacks generally recover no more than from a model that never learned the information.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set is tested.
No activation-direction ablation is tested, and the study does not conclude that the methods merely block access rather than delete information.
The study tests semantically rewritten queries and probabilistic input/output sampling, not jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
CEL is evaluated for residual leakage under the paper's FPE related-query setup. It is not tested against quantization, activation ablation, fine-tuning attacks, jailbreaks, or other languages.

statements.correction: Figure 3, Llama-2-Who-is-Harry-Potter on Harry Potter Q&A, keyword-match leakage: greedy shows no leakage; prob. output (sampling only, Scholten et al. 2024 method) shows residual leakage; FPE (rephrasing plus sampling) also finds questions with leakage probability >0.6. Figure only, one model. Rephrasing with greedy decoding is not run.
statements.problem: The statement presents this study as only combining rephrasing with sampling. Its Figure 3 also has a sampling-only arm (prob. output on the original questions) against greedy, so the sampling effect apart from rephrasing is shown here (figure only).
